original_question: Let f be a Hecke-Maass cusp form of level 1 with spectral parameter t_f. Prove the Weyl-strength subconvex estimate L(1/2 + it, f) <<_epsilon ((1 + |t_f - t|)(1 + |t_f + t|))^(1/6 + epsilon) uniformly, including the conductor-dropping regimes where t_f - t or t_f + t is small relative to max{t_f, |t|}.
target_in_paper: Problem (24) in the section "Bounds for L-functions": Weyl-strength subconvexity for L(1/2+it,f) of a level-1 Hecke-Maass cusp form.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the object f (a level-1 Hecke-Maass cusp form), the spectral parameter t_f, the precise Weyl-strength exponent 1/6+ε, the exact conductor-shaped quantity ((1+|t_f-t|)(1+|t_f+t|))^(1/6+ε), and the fact that the difficult missing range is the conductor-dropping regime near t=±t_f.
missing_details: State the quantifiers explicitly: for every ε>0 and every real t.
Define t_f explicitly as the spectral parameter of f (equivalently, the Laplace eigenvalue is 1/4+t_f^2).
Make explicit that L(s,f) is the L-function attached to f.
Clarify the meaning of the Vinogradov notation: the implied constant in ≪_ε depends at most on ε.
Replace the informal phrase "small relative to" with the paper’s exact formulation of the conductor-dropping regime: t_f-t=o(max{t_f,|t|}) or t_f+t=o(max{t_f,|t|}).
refined_question: Can one prove the following Weyl-strength subconvex estimate posed in the paper? Let f be a Hecke-Maass cusp form of level 1 with spectral parameter t_f (so the Laplace eigenvalue is 1/4+t_f^2). Show that for every ε>0 and every t∈R, one has L(1/2+it,f) ≪_ε ((1+|t_f-t|)(1+|t_f+t|))^(1/6+ε), including the conductor-dropping regimes where t_f-t=o(max{t_f,|t|}) or t_f+t=o(max{t_f,|t|}).
justification: The draft is essentially a faithful paraphrase of the paper’s Problem (24), and it should not be broadened beyond that problem. The exact bound, its Weyl-strength exponent, and the explanation about the conductor-dropping regime all appear in Problem (24) itself. Nearby Problems (13) and (14) show that the paper uses t_f to denote the spectral parameter of a level-1 Hecke-Maass form, and Problem (14) uses the same L(1/2+it,f) notation, so they provide the local notation needed to make the question stand-alone. This paper is a problem list, so the official formulation to target is the problem statement itself rather than a theorem or conjecture elsewhere in the paper.
